summary: Describes an on-line hostnames service, part of the discussion with RFCs 606, 608, 623 and 627.

plainLanguage.summary: It describes a service where a computer can look up other computers' names, like a phone directory.

questions: how were computer addresses looked up
how often was the hostnames file updated
subtitle: Where to find a network computer's address by its name.

tldr.problem: On the early ARPANET, people knew computers by names, not numbers, but they needed to send data to the right address.
tldr.mechanism: An online database holds a list of computer names and their addresses, maintained at one central location but copied to secondary sites when needed.
tldr.outcome: Any program can fetch the up-to-date hostnames file via FTP, letting the network grow without coordinating naming everywhere.

today: RFC 625 describes an early stage of what became the Domain Name System (DNS). The manual file-based approach was later replaced by automated DNS, which remains the standard for hostname resolution.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content: RFC 625 states that more than one computer should maintain a copy of the ARPANET's list of hostnames and their addresses. The Network Information Center (NIC) at Stanford Research Institute maintains the official list, and other sites like UCSB are encouraged to keep backup copies.
sections.plainLanguage: The main computer that lists everyone keeps the official copy, but other computers can make backups so you can find addresses from several places.

sections.title: Accessing the Hostnames File
sections.content: The RFC favors using FTP (File Transfer Protocol) to distribute the hostnames file rather than setting up a special server process. The hostnames file is a plain ASCII text file stored at the NIC with the path <NETINFO>HOSTS.TXT. Each site sets up the same login parameters to FTP and gets the latest copy whenever needed.
sections.plainLanguage: Instead of a fancy system, just let people copy the file with a simple file transfer tool that already works.

sections.title: File Format and Updates
sections.content: The hostnames file holds the computer's name, its numeric address, and status information. The NIC plans to add more details over time. The file stays as plain ASCII text for simplicity and easier troubleshooting. Sites are responsible for fetching updates from the NIC regularly, and changes will be added weekly.
sections.plainLanguage: The list is a simple text file with everyone's computer name and address. It changes every week, and sites copy the new version when they need it.

references.text: Kudlick, M. and J. Feinler, "On-line hostnames service", RFC 625, March 1974.
